meta.scope: Venezuela batch 2 — Oil production recovery, external accounts, inflation/exchange-rate stress, education and labour gaps from ENCOVI, remittances/migration effects. Continues under data-quality caution.

candidates.title: Producción petrolera / Oil production
candidates.description: Crude-oil production volumes. Structural backbone of the external accounts and fiscal capacity. Recent recovery from the deep trough of the late 2010s / early 2020s.
candidates.notes: Core external-revenue node. Production has recovered toward the 1.0–1.2 million barrels/day range in recent readings (highest in several years) but remains far below historical peaks. Continuously cited as the primary driver of any macroeconomic rebound.

candidates.title: Petróleos de Venezuela (PDVSA)
candidates.description: State oil company. Producer, exporter and fiscal contributor of the hydrocarbon sector.
candidates.notes: Institutional parent of the oil economy. Operational and financial condition has been central to the external and fiscal crisis; recovery of production is inseparable from PDVSA’s capacity and from external commercial arrangements.

candidates.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
candidates.description: Balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and reserve changes. Publication and detail have varied over the crisis period.
candidates.notes: Core external-accounts product under data-quality stress. Oil exports dominate the goods account; remittances and other secondary income are material supporting flows.

candidates.title: Reservas internacionales / International reserves
candidates.description: Stock of international reserve assets. Key external-buffer indicator under chronic foreign-exchange pressure.
candidates.notes: External-buffer node. Levels remain low relative to historical peaks and to the economy’s import and debt-service needs; exchange-market intervention draws on available reserves.

candidates.title: Tipo de cambio / Exchange rate
candidates.description: Official and parallel exchange rates. Central relative price in a dual (or multi) exchange-rate environment that shapes inflation, real incomes and import access.
candidates.notes: Lived price signal. Large and persistent gaps between official and parallel rates have been a defining feature of the crisis; recent periods show rapid official depreciation and high inflation pass-through.

candidates.title: Cobertura y asistencia escolar (ENCOVI)
candidates.description: School enrolment and attendance indicators from the independent household survey. Complements residual official education statistics.
candidates.notes: Lived education gap. Coverage remains below pre-crisis levels; a large absolute number of children are out of school, and irregular attendance (2–3 days/week) is widespread among those enrolled.

candidates.title: Empleo y ocupación (ENCOVI)
candidates.description: Labour-force participation, occupation and formal/informal employment indicators from ENCOVI. Primary labour-market window under official-data constraints.
candidates.notes: Lived labour market. Occupation rates are low by regional standards; female participation is especially depressed. Formal employment share has risen from crisis lows but remains limited; self-employment and informal work absorb much of the adjustment.

candidates.title: Remesas / Family remittances
candidates.description: Inflows of personal transfers from Venezuelans living abroad. Major secondary-income and household-support flow.
candidates.notes: Lived external support. Remittances partially offset domestic income shortfalls for receiving households; ENCOVI tracks both the share of households that receive them and changes in sending behaviour among the diaspora.

candidates.title: Bonos y transferencias monetarias del Estado
candidates.description: State cash bonuses and transfers that supplement household income alongside CLAP food boxes.
candidates.notes: Lived social-protection node. Coverage is wide but amounts are small in real terms; ENCOVI analysis has noted that transfers are not strongly progressive (non-poor households also receive them).

candidates.title: Faja Petrolífera del Orinoco — resource base
candidates.description: World’s largest known extra-heavy oil resource. Geographic and geological core of Venezuela’s long-run petroleum potential.
candidates.notes: Foundational resource node. Continuously cited as the physical base of proven reserves (order of 300 billion barrels) and of any sustained recovery scenario; requires specialised technology and large investment to develop at scale.

proposed_edges.basis: PDVSA is the institutional producer of the bulk of Venezuelan crude.
Oil exports dominate the goods account of the balance of payments.
The Orinoco Belt is the principal long-run resource base for production and reserves.
Changes in reserve assets appear in the balance of payments.
Exchange-rate depreciation is a primary pass-through channel into consumer prices.
School coverage and attendance indicators are derived from ENCOVI.
Labour-force and employment indicators are derived from ENCOVI.
Remittances are a major secondary-income item in the balance of payments.
State cash bonuses partially offset low monetary income for receiving households.
